sections.h2: What shapes the housing market in Harlan County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Harlan County lies in southeastern Kentucky against the Virginia line. Harlan is the county seat, Cumberland is the largest city, and Benham, Evarts, Loyall and Lynch complete the six incorporated places. Black Mountain, east of Lynch, rises 4,145 feet and is the state's highest point. Three streams, Poor Fork, Clover Fork and Martins Fork, meet at Baxter to start the Cumberland River. It dates to 1819 and carries the name of Silas Harlan, a frontier soldier.

Coal built the economy. The first coal left by rail in 1911, and the population rose from 10,566 in 1910 to 75,275 in 1940. Every count since 1980 has been lower, down to 26,831 in 2020 and an estimated 24,725 in July 2025. Mining jobs dropped from 13,619 in 1950 to 764 by June 2016.

A seller here is entering a market that has shrunk for decades. That affects the price more than it affects the tax bill, but it decides how much cushion a house has when unpaid taxes or repairs come out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: How low are Harlan County home values?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey figures from Census put the typical owned home at $73,700, roughly half of Hancock County's figure and a third of Hardin County's. Owners live in 71.6 percent of the housing, typical rent is $678 a month, typical household income is $41,693, and 29.4 percent of residents live below the poverty line.

The county has 13,136 housing units against 10,731 households, which is about 2,400 more units than households, and the Census recorded zero building permits for 2025. Around one resident in five is past 65, and 21.4 percent of residents under 65 report a disability. Both groups are the ones the Kentucky homestead exemption is written for.

On a $73,700 house the yearly tax bill is small in dollars. The real risk is a string of unpaid years in which interest and fees grow faster than the home's value.

sections.h2: Which Harlan County offices do I deal with?
sections.html:
Each office keeps its own schedule, so call before you drive in.

  • Sheriff: collects the bill. The sheriff's website links to an online public tax lookup. Call for the discount and penalty dates printed on your bill.
  • Property Valuation Administrator: write to P.O. Box 209 in Harlan (ZIP 40831) or call (606) 573-1990 between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.
  • County Clerk: phone (606) 573-3636. Monday it stays open until 6 p.m.; Tuesday through Friday it closes at 4:30; and on the last Saturday of the month, holiday weekends excepted, it opens 9 a.m. to noon.

The clerk's website has a delinquent taxes page and a third party purchaser application. The PVA's website carries the tax roll and a property search showing assessments and owners. Harlan County's fiscal court is led by the county judge executive and five magistrates, one for each of five districts that run from Bledsoe and Pine Mountain to Pathfork.

sections.h2: What is the real estate tax calendar in Harlan County?
sections.html:
The PVA's website posts the state's cycle in a single chart.

How the Kentucky tax year runs for real estate, from the Harlan County PVA chart
StepWhen
Assessment dateJanuary 1
Listing periodJanuary 1 through March 1
Tax roll open for review, conferences with the PVA13 days beginning on the first Monday of May
Appeals board hearingsFive days, beginning 25 to 35 days after review closes
Bills delivered to the sheriffNo later than September 15
Discount paymentsBy November 1
Payments at face valueNovember 2 through December 31
Bills turn delinquentJanuary 1, with 5 percent through January 31
10 percent penalty and 10 percent sheriff add onAfter January 31
Sheriff passes bills to clerkApril 15
Clerk's certificate salesJuly 14 through August 28

A state ordered delay can move a county to a slower plan with 30 days for each stage, so the dates on your own bill control.

sections.h2: How do I question a Harlan County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA. A conference in the May inspection window is mandatory, and when it produces agreement the new value flows into the fall bill.

Without agreement you have until one workday after the window shuts to file at the clerk's office. A three member local board, appointed by the largest city's mayor, the fiscal court and the county judge executive, meets about five weeks after inspection. It must reject a claim that comes with no facts, so gather sales of similar houses and repair estimates beforehand.

At these values an appeal pays off mostly when the PVA's record is wrong about something concrete, such as a bedroom count, a shed that no longer exists, or a fire damaged building still carried at full value.

sections.h2: Does the buyer get the Harlan County bill after closing?
sections.html:
Not automatically. The bill for a year goes to the January 1 owner, so a later sale leaves it in the seller's name for that year. According to the PVA, staff read the recorded deed and mail the bill to the new owner when they can. A buyer without a copy should call the sheriff.

List a mailing address the buyer will check in the deed, since the clerk cannot take a deed without an in care of address for that year's bill. A seller on the homestead exemption should also tell the PVA, since the exemption does not go to the buyer.

sections.h2: What does a Harlan County bill cost once it is delinquent?
sections.html:
A bill still open when April 15 closes passes to the County Clerk, and a monthly 1 percent interest charge starts. The Department of Revenue's example uses a $1,000 bill.

  • On transfer, with the penalty, sheriff add on and an assumed commission: $1,254.00.
  • Paid within five business days: $1,387.79.
  • Paid after the county attorney's first notice: $1,611.30.
  • Paid after the June advertisement: $1,659.90.

Notices come by mail, and installment plans can be requested before a certificate is sold. If a third party buys it, the owner pays that buyer, who can add substantial fees.

An owner with unpaid years can still sell. The closing agent gets the payoff from the clerk and pays it from the proceeds. A cash offer on an older house can be weighed against a listing by comparing what is left after the payoff.

sections.h2: Which schools and nearby places affect a Harlan County sale?
sections.html:
Two public districts operate here. Harlan Independent Schools serves the city of Harlan, and Harlan County Public Schools covers the rest, with Harlan County High School in the Rosspoint area east of Harlan. Southeast Kentucky Community and Technical College has its main campus in Cumberland.

Part of Cumberland Gap National Historical Park and the Blanton Forest preserve lie in the county, so a house near them may draw outdoor minded buyers. School district boundaries, city limits and fire protection can change the taxes on a bill, so ask the sheriff which districts appear on yours.

faqs.q: What is the last day for the Harlan County discount?
faqs.a: November 1. After that, the chart lists face value through the end of December and a 5 percent penalty in January.

faqs.q: How much extra does a February payment cost in Harlan County?
faqs.a: Ten percent in penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff add on, both of which start once January ends. The state describes the total as 21 percent.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about my Harlan County assessed value?
faqs.a: The PVA at (606) 573-1990 handles the conference that must come before any appeal.

faqs.q: Where do I check for delinquent Harlan County taxes?
faqs.a: The County Clerk's website has a delinquent taxes page, and the clerk's office answers at (606) 573-3636. The sheriff hands over bills after April 15.

faqs.q: Can a Harlan County owner under 65 get the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes, if totally disabled. The statute, KRS 132.810, opens the exemption to age 65 and up, or total disability, for owners living in the home, filed with the PVA.
